LCC.label: Land Cover Components
LCC.tip: Groups the physical things that cover the ground surface, such as buildings, bare rock, plants and water, regardless of what people use the land for.

LCC-1.label: Abiotic, Non-Vegetated Surfaces and Objects
LCC-1.tip: Surfaces without plants, either built by people (e.g. roads, buildings) or made of natural materials like rock, sand or soil.

LCC-1_1.label: Artificial Surfaces and Constructions
LCC-1_1.tip: Places where people have replaced the natural ground with built structures or artificial materials, e.g. towns, roads and industrial sites. Urban parks and other greenery are not counted here.

LCC-1_1_1.label: Sealed Artificial Surfaces and Constructions
LCC-1_1_1.tip: Ground covered by buildings or by hard surfaces such as concrete, asphalt or paving that water cannot soak through, e.g. houses and pavements.

LCC-1_1_1_1.label: Buildings
LCC-1_1_1_1.tip: Permanent roofed structures that shelter people, animals or goods, or house production and services, e.g. homes, barns or factories.

LCC-1_1_1_1_1.label: Conventional Buildings
LCC-1_1_1_1_1.tip: Ordinary medium or large buildings where people live, work or do business, e.g. houses, blocks of flats, offices, shops, farm buildings and factories.

LCC-1_1_1_1_2.label: Specific Buildings
LCC-1_1_1_1_2.tip: Buildings of notable size, height or shape that stand out as landmarks, e.g. stadiums, churches, towers or large greenhouses.

LCC-1_1_1_2.label: Specific Structures and Facilities
LCC-1_1_1_2.tip: Free-standing human-made structures that are not buildings, e.g. bridges, chimneys, pylons, storage tanks, pipelines or solar panels.

LCC-1_1_1_3.label: Open Sealed Surfaces
LCC-1_1_1_3.tip: Flat ground covered with a hard surface like asphalt or concrete that water cannot soak through, e.g. paved roads, car parks, squares and airport runways.

LCC-1_1_2.label: Non-Sealed Artificial Surfaces
LCC-1_1_2.tip: Human-made surfaces that are not paved or built on and still let water soak through, e.g. gravel areas or dumped waste, though plants may still struggle to grow.

LCC-1_1_2_1.label: Open Non-Sealed Artificial Surfaces
LCC-1_1_2_1.tip: Flat open areas surfaced by people with loose or compacted material that still lets water through, e.g. gravel squares, crushed stone, earth sports fields or grass pavers.

LCC-1_1_2_2.label: Waste Materials
LCC-1_1_2_2.tip: Ground covered by discarded material such as household or industrial waste, e.g. construction rubble, slag, scrap metal or wood.

LCC-1_2.label: Natural Material Surfaces
LCC-1_2.tip: Bare surfaces made of natural materials kept in their natural form, whether or not people have affected them, e.g. rock, sand or soil.

LCC-1_2_1.label: Consolidated Surfaces
LCC-1_2_1.tip: Natural solid stone surfaces with no plant cover, forming a continuous hard layer that lets little water through, e.g. exposed bedrock.

LCC-1_2_1_1.label: Bare Rock
LCC-1_2_1_1.tip: Exposed solid rock with only a few cracks or small patches of soil, e.g. rock outcrops, fresh lava flows or quarry faces.

LCC-1_2_1_2.label: Hard Pan
LCC-1_2_1_2.tip: Soil surfaces that have hardened permanently through chemical or physical processes, forming a crust that water and plant roots cannot get through.

LCC-1_2_2.label: Unconsolidated Surfaces
LCC-1_2_2.tip: Ground made of loose mineral particles of any size, laid down by nature or by people, e.g. beaches, sand dunes, scree slopes or river gravel banks.

LCC-1_2_2_1.label: Mineral Fragments
LCC-1_2_2_1.tip: Loose pieces of rock produced as larger rock breaks down over time and then piled up by nature or people; further split by particle size.

LCC-1_2_2_1_1.label: Boulders, Stones
LCC-1_2_2_1_1.tip: Large rock pieces, roughly 20 to 200 cm or bigger, too heavy for people to carry far and moved only by gravity, glaciers or major floods.

LCC-1_2_2_1_2.label: Pebbles, Gravel, Tuff
LCC-1_2_2_1_2.tip: Medium-sized rock pieces between about 2 and 20 cm, moved and piled up by erosion, e.g. scree on mountain slopes or gravel river banks.

LCC-1_2_2_1_3.label: Sand, Grit
LCC-1_2_2_1_3.tip: Small loose grains between 0.06 mm and 2 cm that wind and water can shift, e.g. sand dunes, sandy beaches or volcanic ash.

LCC-1_2_2_1_4.label: Clay, Silt
LCC-1_2_2_1_4.tip: Very fine mineral particles smaller than 0.06 mm that wind and water can easily move, e.g. muddy river banks or fine volcanic ash.

LCC-1_2_2_1_5.label: Mixed Unsorted Material
LCC-1_2_2_1_5.tip: A jumble of unsorted rock material ranging from fine dust to large boulders, most often debris left behind by glaciers.

LCC-1_2_2_2.label: Bare Soils
LCC-1_2_2_2.tip: Soil that could support plants because it holds enough mineral and organic matter, but has no plant cover when observed, e.g. a freshly ploughed field.

LCC-1_2_2_3.label: Natural Deposits
LCC-1_2_2_3.tip: Natural material that builds up over time, either as minerals left when water evaporates or as plant remains that have not fully rotted, e.g. salt crusts or peat.

LCC-1_2_2_3_1.label: Inorganic Deposits
LCC-1_2_2_3_1.tip: Mineral layers left behind when water evaporates, such as salt or gypsum, e.g. the crust on a dried-out salt lake.

LCC-1_2_2_3_2.label: Organic Deposits, Peat
LCC-1_2_2_3_2.tip: Layers of partly rotted plant material, mostly bog moss, that build up in waterlogged wetlands where lack of oxygen slows decay.

LCC-2.label: Biotic, Vegetation
LCC-2.tip: Any ground covered by plants, whether wild, semi-natural or planted by people, e.g. forests, crops or city parks; subdivided by plant type.

LCC-2_1.label: Woody Vegetation
LCC-2_1.tip: Plants with stems made of wood that survive from year to year, such as trees and shrubs; leaf type and whether they lose their leaves are recorded separately.

LCC-2_1_1.label: Trees
LCC-2_1_1.tip: Long-lived woody plants with a single main trunk that branches out, e.g. oaks, pines, fruit trees or ornamental trees. Giant bamboo is not included.

LCC-2_1_2.label: Bushes, Shrubs
LCC-2_1_2.tip: Woody plants with several stems growing from at or near the ground, usually under 5 metres tall, e.g. hawthorn or juniper.

LCC-2_1_2_1.label: Regular Bushes
LCC-2_1_2_1.tip: Ordinary shrubs with several stems from the base and an open, spreading shape, usually under 5 metres tall, e.g. hedgerow bushes.

LCC-2_1_2_2.label: Dwarf Shrubs
LCC-2_1_2_2.tip: Very low woody plants, usually no taller than 25 cm, that thrive in harsh alpine, arctic or dry places, e.g. heather, bilberry or rosemary.

LCC-2_2.label: Herbaceous Vegetation
LCC-2_2.tip: Non-woody plants whose above-ground parts die back at the end of the growing season and regrow from roots, bulbs or seeds, e.g. grasses and wildflowers.

LCC-2_2_1.label: Graminoids, Grass-Like
LCC-2_2_1.tip: Grasses and grass-like plants with narrow leaves growing from the base, including true grasses, sedges and rushes, whether wild or farmed, e.g. lawns, meadows or cereal crops.

LCC-2_2_1_1.label: Grasses, Sedges, Rushes, Cereals
LCC-2_2_1_1.tip: Wild or cultivated grass-like plants that do not grow taller than about 2 metres, e.g. meadow grasses, sedges, rushes or wheat. Reeds and bamboo are not included.

LCC-2_2_1_1_1.label: Poaceae, Grasses, Cereals
LCC-2_2_1_1_1.tip: Members of the true grass family, wild or cultivated, e.g. pasture grasses, lawn turf, or cereals such as wheat, barley and maize.

LCC-2_2_1_1_2.label: Cyperaceae, Sedges, Rushes
LCC-2_2_1_1_2.tip: Sedges and rushes, grass-like plants often found in marshes, wet meadows and other damp places, e.g. cotton grass or soft rush.

LCC-2_2_1_2.label: Reeds, Bamboos, Canes
LCC-2_2_1_2.tip: Tall grass-like plants that can grow higher than 2 metres, e.g. common reed, tall bamboo species or sugar cane.

LCC-2_2_2.label: Non-Graminoids, Forbs, Ferns
LCC-2_2_2.tip: Non-woody plants that are not grasses, such as wildflowers, ferns and many farm crops, e.g. sunflowers, vegetables, strawberries or hops.

LCC-2_3.label: Succulents, Cacti
LCC-2_3.tip: Plants that store water in thick leaves, stems or roots to survive dry or salty conditions, e.g. cacti, stonecrops or glasswort on salt marshes.

LCC-2_4.label: Lichens, Mosses, Algae
LCC-2_4.tip: Small, simple plant-like organisms such as lichens, mosses and algae, which grow on rocks, soil, tree bark or in water.

LCC-2_4_1.label: Lichens
LCC-2_4_1.tip: Crusty, leafy or bushy growths formed by a fungus living together with algae or bacteria, e.g. the grey-green patches on rocks and tree bark.

LCC-2_4_2.label: Mosses
LCC-2_4_2.tip: Small, non-woody plants only a few centimetres tall, without true roots, that take in water and nutrients mainly through their leaves, e.g. bog moss.

LCC-2_4_3.label: Algae
LCC-2_4_3.tip: A large, varied group of simple plant-like organisms that mostly live in or near water, though some grow on damp rocks or tree trunks.

LCC-2_4_3_1.label: Macro Algae
LCC-2_4_3_1.tip: Large algae with branching, leaf-like shapes that can grow several metres long, rooted underwater or floating, e.g. seaweed or kelp.

LCC-2_4_3_2.label: Micro Algae, Plankton
LCC-2_4_3_2.tip: Tiny single-celled or small clustered algae, usually living in water as plankton but also as green films on rocks or tree trunks.

LCC-3.label: Water
LCC-3.tip: Surfaces covered by water in any form, either liquid (e.g. rivers, lakes, sea) or frozen (snow and ice).

LCC-3_1.label: Liquid Water Bodies
LCC-3_1.tip: Water in its liquid form, whatever its shape, saltiness or origin, in a fairly stable bed, e.g. rivers, lakes or the sea. Areas only briefly flooded are not included.

LCC-3_1_1.label: Inland Water Bodies
LCC-3_1_1.tip: Inland water surfaces not directly connected to the open sea, whether fresh or salty, natural or human-made, e.g. rivers, lakes and reservoirs.

LCC-3_1_1_1.label: Water Course
LCC-3_1_1_1.tip: Flowing water such as rivers, streams, creeks or canals.

LCC-3_1_1_2.label: Standing Water
LCC-3_1_1_2.tip: Still, non-flowing water, mainly lakes and ponds, e.g. natural lakes, fishponds, reservoirs or cut-off river bends (oxbow lakes).

LCC-3_1_2.label: Marine Waters
LCC-3_1_2.tip: Sea water on the seaward side of the average high-tide line, including tidal flats along coasts that flood and drain with the tides.

LCC-3_2.label: Solid Waters
LCC-3_2.tip: Water in frozen form, such as snow, ice and glaciers.

LCC-3_2_1.label: Snow
LCC-3_2_1.tip: Ground covered by snow, e.g. snowfields on high mountains that remain all year.

LCC-3_2_2.label: Ice, Glaciers
LCC-3_2_2.tip: Ground covered by ice, including glaciers formed as snow piles up and compacts into ice over many years.

LUA.label: Land Use Attributes
LUA.tip: Groups the ways people use land, such as farming, industry, services, transport or housing. An area can carry several uses, recorded at the most detailed level known.

LUA-1.label: Primary Production Sector
LUA-1.tip: Land used to produce goods directly from local natural resources, e.g. farming, forestry, fishing, mining and quarrying, plus nearby first-stage processing.

LUA-1_1.label: Agriculture
LUA-1_1.tip: Land used to grow crops or raise animals for food, sale, own use or industry, including greenhouses, fallow fields and biofuel crops.

LUA-1_1_1.label: Commercial Crop Production
LUA-1_1_1.tip: Fields, orchards and grasslands farmed to produce crops or fodder for people, livestock, bioenergy or industry, in the open or in greenhouses.

LUA-1_1_2.label: Farming Infrastructure
LUA-1_1_2.tip: Buildings and facilities on farms, e.g. farmhouses, animal sheds, manure stores and buildings for handling or processing crops.

LUA-1_1_2_1.label: Animal Husbandry
LUA-1_1_2_1.tip: Farm facilities for housing and feeding livestock, e.g. cattle sheds, poultry houses or pig barns; also covers insects and land snails.

LUA-1_1_2_2.label: Farming Storage
LUA-1_1_2_2.tip: Farm areas or buildings used for storage, e.g. barns or maize silage clamps.

LUA-1_1_2_3.label: Other Farming Infrastructure
LUA-1_1_2_3.tip: Farm facilities other than animal housing or storage, used for handling and processing crops and similar tasks, e.g. a grain drying or sorting shed.

LUA-1_1_3.label: Production for Own Consumption
LUA-1_1_3.tip: Land where people grow food or keep animals for their own household rather than for sale, e.g. kitchen gardens or private animal sheds.

LUA-1_2.label: Forestry
LUA-1_2.tip: Land used to grow and harvest wood, e.g. timber, firewood or pulpwood, including tree nurseries and log storage areas, in natural or planted forests.

LUA-1_3.label: Mining and Quarrying
LUA-1_3.tip: Land used to extract naturally occurring materials such as coal, ores, gravel, sand, salt, oil, natural gas or peat, above or below ground.

LUA-1_4.label: Aquaculture and Fishing
LUA-1_4.tip: Areas used for commercial fishing and for farming fish and other water animals.

LUA-1_4_1.label: Aquaculture
LUA-1_4_1.tip: Areas used to breed and rear fish and other water animals, e.g. fish hatcheries, mussel farms or crocodile farms.

LUA-1_4_2.label: Professional Wild Fishery
LUA-1_4_2.tip: Water areas used for commercial catching of wild fish and seafood, typically offshore.

LUA-1_5.label: Other Primary Production
LUA-1_5.tip: Primary production not covered by farming, forestry, mining or fishing, e.g. commercial hunting, gathering wild products, herding migratory animals or beekeeping.

LUA-1_5_1.label: Hunting
LUA-1_5_1.tip: Areas, fenced or open, used for professional hunting of wild animals.

LUA-1_5_2.label: Management of Migratory Animals
LUA-1_5_2.tip: Areas used for keeping and feeding animals that roam over large ranges, such as reindeer or deer.

LUA-1_5_3.label: Picking Natural Products
LUA-1_5_3.tip: Areas where wild, uncultivated products other than wood are gathered for sale, e.g. wild berries, mosses or lichens.

LUA-1_5_4.label: Apiculture, Bee Hives
LUA-1_5_4.tip: Areas used for honey production, with one or more bee colonies present; like hunting, its outer boundary is often hard to draw.

LUA-2.label: Secondary Production Sector
LUA-2.tip: Land used by industry to turn raw materials into finished or part-finished goods, e.g. factories, plus their linked storage and transport areas.

LUA-2_1.label: Manufacturing Industry
LUA-2_1.tip: Groups factory-based production of goods, split into raw materials industry, heavy products and light products.

LUA-2_1_1.label: Raw Industry
LUA-2_1_1.tip: Industry that turns farm, forest and mining output into basic manufactured materials, e.g. sawmills, steelworks or chemical plants.

LUA-2_1_1_1.label: Manufacturing Textile Products
LUA-2_1_1_1.tip: Sites used for preparing and spinning fibres, weaving fabric, making thread, and tanning or dressing leather, e.g. a textile mill.

LUA-2_1_1_2.label: Manufacturing Wood-Based Products
LUA-2_1_1_2.tip: Sites that process wood into products, e.g. sawmills and plants making plywood, fibreboard, joinery, cork or straw goods.

LUA-2_1_1_3.label: Manufacturing Pulp and Paper Products
LUA-2_1_1_3.tip: Sites used for making pulp, paper, cardboard, paper-based hygiene products or wallpaper, e.g. a paper mill.

LUA-2_1_1_4.label: Manufacturing Coke, Petroleum And Nuclear Fuels
LUA-2_1_1_4.tip: Sites used for producing coke, refining petroleum or processing nuclear fuel, e.g. an oil refinery.

LUA-2_1_1_5.label: Manufacturing Chemical Products and Synthetic Fibres
LUA-2_1_1_5.tip: Sites making chemicals and synthetic fibres, e.g. fertilisers, paints, medicines, soap, glue or nylon. Natural fibres like cotton or flax are not included.

LUA-2_1_1_6.label: Manufacturing Metallic Products
LUA-2_1_1_6.tip: Sites used for producing, processing and casting iron, steel and other metals, and for making metal products, e.g. a steelworks or foundry.

LUA-2_1_1_7.label: Manufacturing Nonmetallic Mineral Products
LUA-2_1_1_7.tip: Sites making glass, bricks, ceramics, cement, concrete, lime or plaster, or cutting and shaping stone, e.g. a brickworks.

LUA-2_1_1_8.label: Manufacturing Rubber and Plastic Products
LUA-2_1_1_8.tip: Sites used for making tyres, tubes, plastic packaging and other rubber or plastic goods.

LUA-2_1_1_9.label: Manufacturing Other Raw Materials
LUA-2_1_1_9.tip: Sites producing basic manufactured materials that do not fit any of the other raw industry categories.

LUA-2_1_2.label: Heavy End Product Industry
LUA-2_1_2.tip: Industry that turns basic manufactured materials into heavy finished products such as machinery and vehicles.

LUA-2_1_2_1.label: Manufacturing Machinery Products
LUA-2_1_2_1.tip: Sites making machines for industry, farming, forestry and other uses, as well as weapons, ammunition and household appliances (but not vehicles or aircraft).

LUA-2_1_2_2.label: Manufacturing Vehicles and Transport Equipment
LUA-2_1_2_2.tip: Sites building vehicles and transport equipment, e.g. car factories, shipyards, or plants making aircraft, trains, motorcycles or bicycles.

LUA-2_1_2_3.label: Manufacturing Other Heavy End Products
LUA-2_1_2_3.tip: Sites making heavy finished products that do not fit the machinery or vehicle categories.

LUA-2_1_3.label: Light End Product Industry
LUA-2_1_3.tip: Industry that turns basic manufactured materials into lighter consumer goods, e.g. food, clothing, electronics or furniture.

LUA-2_1_3_1.label: Manufacturing Food, Beverages and Tobacco Products
LUA-2_1_3_1.tip: Sites that process food, drinks and tobacco, e.g. meat and dairy plants, flour mills, breweries or animal feed factories.

LUA-2_1_3_2.label: Manufacturing Clothes and Leather Products
LUA-2_1_3_2.tip: Sites making clothing, fur and leather goods, luggage, bags, saddles and footwear.

LUA-2_1_3_3.label: Publishing, Printing, Reproduction of Recorded Media
LUA-2_1_3_3.tip: Sites used for publishing and printing books, newspapers and journals, and for producing copies of sound recordings.

LUA-2_1_3_4.label: Manufacturing Electrical, Precision and Optical Equipment
LUA-2_1_3_4.tip: Sites making electrical, electronic and precision equipment, e.g. computers, cables, batteries, lamps, phones, medical instruments or watches.

LUA-2_1_3_5.label: Manufacturing Other Light End Products
LUA-2_1_3_5.tip: Sites making other light consumer goods, e.g. furniture, jewellery, musical instruments, sports goods and toys.

LUA-2_2.label: Energy Production
LUA-2_2.tip: Land used to produce electricity or heat, e.g. power stations, wind farms or solar parks.

LUA-2_2_1.label: Nuclear Based Energy Production
LUA-2_2_1.tip: Land where nuclear power plants are operated.

LUA-2_2_2.label: Fossil Fuel Based Energy Production
LUA-2_2_2.tip: Power plants that burn fossil fuels such as coal, oil, natural gas or peat.

LUA-2_2_2_1.label: Coal and Lignite Based Energy Production
LUA-2_2_2_1.tip: Power plants that burn coal or lignite (brown coal) to generate energy.

LUA-2_2_2_2.label: Mineral Oil Based Energy Production
LUA-2_2_2_2.tip: Power plants that burn mineral oil to generate energy.

LUA-2_2_2_3.label: Mineral Gas Based Energy Production
LUA-2_2_2_3.tip: Power plants that burn natural gas to generate energy.

LUA-2_2_2_4.label: Peat and Other Fossil Fuel Based Energy Production
LUA-2_2_2_4.tip: Power plants that burn peat or other fossil fuels not covered by the coal, oil or gas categories.

LUA-2_2_3.label: Biomass Based Energy Production
LUA-2_2_3.tip: Power plants that burn fuels made from plants or organic matter, e.g. wood, biogas or other biofuels.

LUA-2_2_4.label: Renewable Energy Production
LUA-2_2_4.tip: Land used to produce energy from renewable sources other than biomass, e.g. hydropower, solar, wind, geothermal, tidal or wave power.

LUA-2_2_4_1.label: Water Based Energy Production
LUA-2_2_4_1.tip: Areas that generate electricity by letting river currents or water falling from reservoirs turn turbines, e.g. hydroelectric dams. Tidal power is not included.

LUA-2_2_4_2.label: Solar Based Energy Production
LUA-2_2_4_2.tip: Areas that collect sunlight to produce electricity or heat using solar panels or solar heat collectors, on land or floating on water.

LUA-2_2_4_3.label: Wind Based Energy Production
LUA-2_2_4_3.tip: Areas on land or offshore that generate electricity with wind turbines, e.g. a wind farm.

LUA-2_2_4_4.label: Geo-Thermal Based Energy Production
LUA-2_2_4_4.tip: Areas that produce heat or electricity using the natural heat from deep underground, e.g. a geothermal power station.

LUA-2_2_4_5.label: Tide Based Energy Production
LUA-2_2_4_5.tip: Coastal areas that generate electricity by using tidal currents to turn turbines.

LUA-2_2_5.label: Waste Combustion Based Energy Production
LUA-2_2_5.tip: Areas where energy is produced by burning waste, e.g. a waste-to-energy incinerator.

LUA-2_5.label: Other Industry
LUA-2_5.tip: Land used to make industrial products that do not fit any of the other industry or energy categories.

LUA-3.label: Tertiary Services Sector
LUA-3.tip: Land used to provide services to businesses and the public, e.g. shops, offices, hotels, schools, hospitals, government buildings and leisure facilities.

LUA-3_1.label: Commercial Services
LUA-3_1.tip: Land used to provide commercial services, such as shops, real estate, hotels and restaurants.

LUA-3_1_1.label: Wholesale, Retail Trade, Repair of Vehicles and Household Goods
LUA-3_1_1.tip: Land used for buying and selling goods wholesale or retail and for repairing vehicles and household items, e.g. shops, car dealers or repair workshops.

LUA-3_1_2.label: Real Estate Services
LUA-3_1_2.tip: Land used for real estate and renting services, e.g. estate agency or property rental offices.

LUA-3_1_3.label: Accommodation and Food Services
LUA-3_1_3.tip: Land used for places to stay and eat, e.g. hotels, holiday villages, campsites, restaurants, bars and canteens.

LUA-3_1_4.label: Other Commercial Services
LUA-3_1_4.tip: Commercial services not covered elsewhere, e.g. beauty salons, spas or other wellbeing services.

LUA-3_2.label: Financial, Professional and Information Services
LUA-3_2.tip: Land used to provide financial, professional or information services, typically in offices.

LUA-3_2_1.label: Financial and Insurance Services
LUA-3_2_1.tip: Land used for banking, lending, insurance and other financial services, e.g. bank branches or insurance offices.

LUA-3_2_2.label: Professional, Technical and Scientific Services
LUA-3_2_2.tip: Land used for expert services such as IT, research and development, law, accounting, architecture, engineering, advertising or consulting.

LUA-3_2_3.label: Information and Communication Services
LUA-3_2_3.tip: Land used for media and communication services, e.g. publishing, film and TV production, radio broadcasting, post, telecoms and data processing.

LUA-3_2_4.label: Administrative and Support Services
LUA-3_2_4.tip: Land used for support services to businesses and people, e.g. travel agencies, rental firms, cleaning or security companies.

LUA-3_2_5.label: Other Financial Professional and Information Services
LUA-3_2_5.tip: Financial, professional or information services that do not fit any of the other categories in this group.

LUA-3_3.label: Community Services
LUA-3_3.tip: Land used to provide services to the community, e.g. public administration, schools, hospitals and religious sites.

LUA-3_3_1.label: Public Administration, Defense, Justice, Public Security
LUA-3_3_1.tip: Land used for government administration, defence, courts, police, fire services and compulsory social security, e.g. town halls or military bases.

LUA-3_3_2.label: Science, Research, Education
LUA-3_3_2.tip: Land used for education at all levels, from primary schools to universities and adult education.

LUA-3_3_3.label: Health and Social Services
LUA-3_3_3.tip: Land used for health care and social work for people and animals, e.g. hospitals, clinics, care homes or veterinary practices.

LUA-3_3_4.label: Religious Services
LUA-3_3_4.tip: Land used for religious purposes, e.g. places of worship, monasteries and cemeteries.

LUA-3_3_4_1.label: House of Worship
LUA-3_3_4_1.tip: Buildings for religious worship of any faith, e.g. churches, mosques or synagogues, including their associated administrative buildings.

LUA-3_3_4_2.label: Monastery
LUA-3_3_4_2.tip: Monasteries, where a community of people lives together to devote their lives to practising their religion according to set rules and rituals.

LUA-3_3_4_3.label: Cemetery
LUA-3_3_4_3.tip: Burial grounds of any faith, including historical cemeteries.

LUA-3_3_5.label: Other Community Services
LUA-3_3_5.tip: Land used for community services not covered by the other categories, e.g. cemeteries.

LUA-3_4.label: Cultural, Entertainment and Recreational Services
LUA-3_4.tip: Land used for culture, entertainment, sport and recreation, e.g. museums, theme parks, stadiums and city parks.

LUA-3_4_1.label: Cultural Services
LUA-3_4_1.tip: Land used for arts, libraries, museums, zoos, botanical gardens, historical sites and other cultural services.

LUA-3_4_1_1.label: Indoor Cultural Service
LUA-3_4_1_1.tip: Indoor venues for culture, e.g. libraries, museums and theatres.

LUA-3_4_1_2.label: Outdoor Cultural Service
LUA-3_4_1_2.tip: Outdoor places for culture, e.g. zoos and botanical gardens.

LUA-3_4_2.label: Entertainment
LUA-3_4_2.tip: Land used for entertainment, e.g. amusement parks, theme parks and casinos or other gambling venues.

LUA-3_4_3.label: Sports Infrastructure
LUA-3_4_3.tip: Land used for sports facilities, e.g. stadiums, sports halls, swimming pools, gyms, ski resorts and golf courses.

LUA-3_4_3_2.label: Ski Piste
LUA-3_4_3_2.tip: Prepared slopes used for alpine skiing, snowboarding and other snow sliding sports.

LUA-3_4_3_3.label: Outdoor Racecourse
LUA-3_4_3_3.tip: Outdoor tracks for racing, e.g. motor racing circuits, motocross or mountain bike courses, horse racecourses and skate parks.

LUA-3_4_3_4.label: Sport Hall
LUA-3_4_3_4.tip: Indoor halls big enough for team ball games such as basketball, volleyball or handball.

LUA-3_4_3_5.label: Stadium
LUA-3_4_3_5.tip: Sports grounds (grass, sand, artificial turf, etc.) surrounded by covered or open stands for spectators, e.g. a football stadium.

LUA-3_4_3_6.label: Swimming Pool
LUA-3_4_3_6.tip: Indoor swimming halls and outdoor swimming pools.

LUA-3_4_3_7.label: Sports Ground
LUA-3_4_3_7.tip: Outdoor sports fields without a roof or spectator stands around them, e.g. a local football pitch or athletics track.

LUA-3_4_3_8.label: Fitness Club
LUA-3_4_3_8.tip: Indoor gyms and clubs for fitness and individual sports such as boxing, wrestling, body workouts or gymnastics, smaller than full sports halls.

LUA-3_4_3_9.label: Yachtharbour, Sport Boat Marina
LUA-3_4_3_9.tip: Harbours for leisure boats and yachts, covering the land areas and, where relevant, the harbour water itself.

LUA-3_4_4.label: Open Air Recreational Areas
LUA-3_4_4.tip: Outdoor areas used for leisure, from city parks and playgrounds to national parks and countryside such as forests, moors, lakes and mountains.

LUA-3_4_4_1.label: Urban Greenery, City Parks, Playgrounds
LUA-3_4_4_1.tip: Green spaces in towns used for leisure, e.g. city parks, playgrounds and other urban greenery.

LUA-3_4_4_2.label: (Semi-)Natural Areas Used for Recreation
LUA-3_4_4_2.tip: Natural or near-natural areas used for leisure, e.g. national parks, forests, heaths, mountains, lakes or rivers used for walking and recreation.

LUA-3_4_5.label: Other Recreational Services
LUA-3_4_5.tip: Recreational uses not covered by the other culture, entertainment and recreation categories, e.g. allotments or hobby fishing.

LUA-3_4_5_1.label: Allotment Garden
LUA-3_4_5_1.tip: Small plots of land in towns rented as gardens, sometimes for growing food but mainly for leisure.

LUA-3_4_5_2.label: Amateur Fishing
LUA-3_4_5_2.tip: Ponds, lakes, rivers and nearby land used for hobby fishing, mainly inland. Offshore fishing is not included.

LUA-3_5.label: Other Services
LUA-3_5.tip: Land used for services that do not fit any of the other service categories.

LUA-4.label: Transport Networks, Logistics, Utilities
LUA-4.tip: Land used for the basic networks society depends on, e.g. transport, storage, communications, water supply and sewage or waste treatment.

LUA-4_1.label: Transport Networks
LUA-4_1.tip: Land used for transport infrastructure, such as roads, railways, airports and ports.

LUA-4_1_1.label: Road Network
LUA-4_1_1.tip: Land used for road transport, e.g. roads, car parks and service stations.

LUA-4_1_2.label: Railway Network
LUA-4_1_2.tip: Land used for rail transport, e.g. tracks, railway stations and rail yards.

LUA-4_1_3.label: Air Transport
LUA-4_1_3.tip: Land used for air transport, e.g. airports and their related services.

LUA-4_1_4.label: Water Transport
LUA-4_1_4.tip: Land and water used for shipping and boat transport, e.g. ports, docks and navigable rivers.

LUA-4_1_5.label: Other Transportation Networks
LUA-4_1_5.tip: Land used for forms of transport that do not fit the road, rail, air or water transport categories.

LUA-4_2.label: Logistics and Storage
LUA-4_2.tip: Land used to store industrial or trade goods away from factory sites, plus the facilities that support this, e.g. warehouses and distribution centres.

LUA-4_3.label: Utilities
LUA-4_3.tip: Land used for public services that keep a place running, such as power and water supply, sewage handling and waste treatment.

LUA-4_3_1.label: Power Distribution Services
LUA-4_3_1.tip: Areas used to deliver energy, such as electricity lines, gas networks and district heating, including pipelines that carry oil and gas.

LUA-4_3_1_1.label: Electricity Distribution
LUA-4_3_1_1.tip: Land used to move electricity to users, e.g. the corridors of power lines and the sites of electrical substations.

LUA-4_3_1_2.label: Gas Distribution
LUA-4_3_1_2.tip: Land used to distribute gas to users, e.g. gas pipeline routes and their associated stations.

LUA-4_3_1_3.label: Thermal Energy Distribution
LUA-4_3_1_3.tip: Land used to distribute heat to buildings, e.g. the pipes and facilities of a district heating network.

LUA-4_3_2.label: Water and Sewage Infrastructure
LUA-4_3_2.tip: Areas used to supply clean water and deal with sewage, from extraction and purification to storage, distribution and wastewater treatment, pipelines included.

LUA-4_3_2_1.label: Drinking Water Facilities
LUA-4_3_2_1.tip: Facilities and their grounds for getting, treating, storing and distributing drinking water, e.g. a waterworks or a water reservoir site.

LUA-4_3_2_2.label: Sewage Water Treatment
LUA-4_3_2_2.tip: Sites where wastewater from homes and businesses is cleaned before release, e.g. a municipal sewage treatment plant.

LUA-4_3_2_3.label: Water Runoff Retention Basin
LUA-4_3_2_3.tip: Basins built to hold back runoff water in a stream so that the risk of flooding downstream is reduced.

LUA-4_3_2_4.label: Artificial Snow Water Pond
LUA-4_3_2_4.tip: Ponds kept in ski resort areas to store water that is used for making artificial snow.

LUA-4_3_2_5.label: Irrigation and Fire Fighting Water Pond
LUA-4_3_2_5.tip: Basins that store water for putting out fires or for watering farmland, and sometimes forest land.

LUA-4_3_3.label: Waste Treatment
LUA-4_3_3.tip: Areas where waste is collected, treated or recycled, e.g. landfills, incinerators, composting sites and hazardous waste plants.

LUA-4_3_3_1.label: Dump Site
LUA-4_3_3_1.tip: Areas where waste is collected and deposited, such as a landfill or rubbish tip.

LUA-4_3_3_1_1.label: Hazardous Waste
LUA-4_3_3_1_1.tip: Waste that can harm people or nature and needs special handling or sealed sites. What counts as hazardous depends partly on national law.

LUA-4_3_3_1_2.label: Inert Or Non-Hazardous Waste
LUA-4_3_3_1_2.tip: Waste that poses no danger to people or the environment, e.g. construction rubble and normal household rubbish.

LUA-4_3_3_2.label: Recycling Facilities
LUA-4_3_3_2.tip: Sites where used materials are prepared for reuse, e.g. paper, plastic bottles and glass, or garden waste turned into compost.

LUA-4_3_4.label: Other Utilities
LUA-4_3_4.tip: Land used for utility services that do not fit into the energy, water, sewage or waste categories.

LUA-5.label: Residential
LUA-5.tip: Land used mainly for people's homes, from city apartment blocks to rural houses and mobile homes, including areas mixed with compatible uses.

LUA-5_1.label: Permanent Residential
LUA-5_1.tip: Housing areas where people live all year round, e.g. detached houses with gardens, terraced rows or blocks of flats.

LUA-5_2.label: Residential Use With Other Compatible Uses
LUA-5_2.tip: Housing areas mixed with other uses that sit well alongside homes, e.g. local shops, services or light workshops.

LUA-5_3.label: Other Residential
LUA-5_3.tip: Housing that is not a permanent main residence, such as holiday cottages, temporary camps or informal settlements.

LUA-5_3_1.label: Temporary Residential, Permanent Structure
LUA-5_3_1.tip: Solid buildings used only part of the year as homes, e.g. summer cottages or holiday houses.

LUA-5_3_2.label: Temporary Dwelling, Non-Permanent Structure
LUA-5_3_2.tip: Areas of temporary shelters that are not built to last, e.g. refugee camps or camps for migrant people.

LUA-5_3_3.label: Informal Dwelling
LUA-5_3_3.tip: Settlements built outside any legal or planning framework, such as slums or favelas, that over time become quasi-permanent.

LUA-6.label: Other Uses
LUA-6.tip: Land that fits none of the main use groups (production, services, transport and utilities, housing), including areas under construction.

LUA-6_1.label: Transitional Areas Under Construction
LUA-6_1.tip: Land where building work is currently under way. Used for actual present use, not for future planned use.

LUA-6_3.label: Areas Not In Any Economic Use
LUA-6_3.tip: Land left in a natural state with no economic use, e.g. untouched wilderness or remote mountain areas.

LUA-6_4.label: Flood Protection
LUA-6_4.tip: Land set aside to reduce flooding, e.g. a polder that can be flooded on purpose to lower a river's flood peak.

LCH.label: Land Characteristics
LCH.tip: Groups extra descriptive details that can be attached to land cover or land use, such as materials, plant traits, water conditions, status, patterns, shape and timing.

LCH-1.label: Built-Up Characteristics
LCH-1.tip: Details that describe built-up areas, such as how much ground is sealed, building layout, construction materials, green roofs and transport features.

LCH-1_1.label: Soil Sealing Degree
LCH-1_1.tip: Measures the share of an area covered by sealed, waterproof surfaces like asphalt, concrete or buildings, given as a percentage (%).

LCH-1_2.label: Built-Up Pattern
LCH-1_2.tip: Groups the typical ways buildings are sized and spread across an area, from scattered farmhouses to dense city blocks.

LCH-1_2_1.label: Scattered Single Houses, Discontinuous
LCH-1_2_1.tip: A few buildings spread out with clear gaps between them, not dominating the landscape, as in sparsely populated countryside.

LCH-1_2_2.label: Single Blocks, Discontinuous
LCH-1_2_2.tip: Large multi-storey buildings standing apart with open space between them, housing many people or offices, e.g. apartment blocks or a skyscraper.

LCH-1_2_3.label: Suburban Row Houses, Terraced, Semi-Detached Houses
LCH-1_2_3.tip: Suburban housing where gardens take up much of each plot, e.g. rows of terraced or semi-detached houses.

LCH-1_2_4.label: City Street Blocks, Closed Front
LCH-1_2_4.tip: City-centre blocks enclosed by streets, with buildings standing wall to wall along the street and mostly paved backyards.

LCH-1_2_5.label: Large Complex Buildings, Big Halls
LCH-1_2_5.tip: Very large stand-alone buildings or halls, e.g. a football stadium, airport terminal, train station or cathedral.

LCH-1_3.label: Building Nature
LCH-1_3.tip: Groups labels for what kind of building something is, based on the INSPIRE buildings standard, e.g. church, silo, lighthouse or greenhouse.

LCH-1_3_1.label: Building Nature Value
LCH-1_3_1.tip: A value naming the specific type of a building, taken from the INSPIRE buildings code list, e.g. chapel, tower or windmill.

LCH-1_4.label: Other Construction Nature
LCH-1_4.tip: Groups labels for man-made structures that are not buildings, e.g. bridges, dams, chimneys, pylons, wind turbines or solar panels.

LCH-1_4_1.label: Other Construction Nature Value
LCH-1_4_1.tip: A value naming the type of a non-building structure, taken from an INSPIRE code list, e.g. antenna, retaining wall or storage tank.

LCH-1_5.label: Artificial Surface Material Type
LCH-1_5.tip: Groups the man-made materials found on ground surfaces and roofs in towns, e.g. concrete, asphalt, metal or roof tiles.

LCH-1_5_1.label: Mineral Compound
LCH-1_5_1.tip: Man-made materials produced from mined earth by mixing components and adding water or heat, e.g. concrete, glass or brick.

LCH-1_5_1_1.label: Glass
LCH-1_5_1_1.tip: Glass used as a surface material, for example on glass roofs or glazed building surfaces.

LCH-1_5_1_2.label: Ceramic, Clay Tiles, Bricks
LCH-1_5_1_2.tip: Fired clay products used on roofs and ground surfaces, e.g. clay roof tiles, ceramic tiles or bricks.

LCH-1_5_1_3.label: Concrete
LCH-1_5_1_3.tip: Concrete used as a surface material, e.g. on pavements, car parks or flat roofs.

LCH-1_5_1_4.label: Asbestos Fibre Cement
LCH-1_5_1_4.tip: Cement boards or sheets reinforced with asbestos fibres, often found on older roofs, e.g. corrugated roofing sheets.

LCH-1_5_1_5.label: Non-Asbestos Fibre Cement
LCH-1_5_1_5.tip: Fibre-reinforced cement boards or sheets made without asbestos, used for example as roofing or cladding.

LCH-1_5_2.label: Solar Panels
LCH-1_5_2.tip: Surfaces covered with solar panels, e.g. photovoltaic panels on a roof or in a solar park.

LCH-1_5_3.label: Metal
LCH-1_5_3.tip: Metal used as a surface material, mainly on roofs, e.g. copper, zinc, aluminium or steel sheeting.

LCH-1_5_3_1.label: Copper
LCH-1_5_3_1.tip: Copper used as a surface material, e.g. a copper roof, often turning green with age.

LCH-1_5_3_2.label: Zinc
LCH-1_5_3_2.tip: Zinc used as a surface material, e.g. zinc roof sheeting.

LCH-1_5_3_3.label: Aluminium
LCH-1_5_3_3.tip: Aluminium used as a surface material, e.g. aluminium roof panels.

LCH-1_5_3_4.label: Steel
LCH-1_5_3_4.tip: Steel used as a surface material, e.g. steel roofing sheets on warehouses or factories.

LCH-1_5_3_5.label: Iron
LCH-1_5_3_5.tip: Iron used as a surface material, e.g. corrugated iron roofing.

LCH-1_5_3_6.label: Lead
LCH-1_5_3_6.tip: Lead used as a surface material, e.g. lead sheeting on roofs.

LCH-1_5_4.label: Hydrocarbon Compound
LCH-1_5_4.tip: Materials made from leftovers of refined crude oil, often mixed with sand or gravel to seal roads and roofs, e.g. asphalt or tar.

LCH-1_5_4_1.label: Tar
LCH-1_5_4_1.tip: Tar, a dark sticky oil-based material used to seal and harden surfaces such as roads or roofs.

LCH-1_5_4_2.label: Asphalt
LCH-1_5_4_2.tip: Asphalt, the dark oil-based mix with gravel or sand commonly used to pave roads and car parks.

LCH-1_5_4_3.label: Bitumen
LCH-1_5_4_3.tip: Bitumen, a thick oil-based binder used to waterproof surfaces, e.g. bitumen roofing felt or road surfacing.

LCH-1_5_5.label: Polymer, Plastic, Synthetic Fibre
LCH-1_5_5.tip: Synthetic materials made industrially by chemical processing, e.g. plastics, rubber and synthetic fibres used on surfaces.

LCH-1_5_5_1.label: Hard Rubber
LCH-1_5_5_1.tip: Hard rubber used as a surface material, e.g. rubber flooring on playgrounds or sports areas.

LCH-1_5_5_2.label: Hard Plastic
LCH-1_5_5_2.tip: Rigid plastic used as a surface material, e.g. plastic roofing panels.

LCH-1_5_5_3.label: Plastic Foil
LCH-1_5_5_3.tip: Thin plastic sheeting covering a surface, e.g. foil over crops or a plastic liner.

LCH-1_5_5_4.label: Synthetic Fibre
LCH-1_5_5_4.tip: Synthetic fibre used as a surface material, e.g. artificial turf on a sports pitch.

LCH-1_5_6.label: Mineral Material
LCH-1_5_6.tip: Natural stone materials taken from quarries, riverbeds, beaches and similar sources, used without chemical processing, e.g. gravel or slate.

LCH-1_5_6_1.label: Natural Stone
LCH-1_5_6_1.tip: Natural stone used as a surface material, e.g. cobblestones or stone slabs.

LCH-1_5_6_2.label: Slate
LCH-1_5_6_2.tip: Slate, a natural stone that splits into thin flat layers, commonly used as roofing on older houses.

LCH-1_5_6_3.label: Pebbles, Gravel
LCH-1_5_6_3.tip: Loose small stones used on surfaces, e.g. a gravel path or pebble-covered roof.

LCH-1_5_6_4.label: Sand
LCH-1_5_6_4.tip: Sand used as a surface material, e.g. on a sports ground or path.

LCH-1_5_6_5.label: Ashes, Slag
LCH-1_5_6_5.tip: Ashes or slag, the leftovers from burning or metal smelting, used as a surface material, e.g. on a cinder track.

LCH-1_5_7.label: Organic
LCH-1_5_7.tip: Surface materials of plant origin used on roofs or the ground, e.g. wooden shingles or thatch.

LCH-1_5_7_1.label: Wood
LCH-1_5_7_1.tip: Wood used as a surface material, e.g. wooden shingles, decking or boardwalks.

LCH-1_5_7_2.label: Reed, Straw, Leaves
LCH-1_5_7_2.tip: Plant stems or leaves used as a surface material, e.g. a thatched roof of reed or straw.

LCH-1_6.label: Artificial Surface Material Arrangement
LCH-1_6.tip: Groups the ways surface materials are laid out on ground or roofs, e.g. a continuous layer, paving stones or overlapping tiles.

LCH-1_6_1.label: Seamless Sealing
LCH-1_6_1.tip: Material laid as one continuous layer with no joints, e.g. an asphalt road surface.

LCH-1_6_2.label: Closed Pavement
LCH-1_6_2.tip: Paving made of separate pieces fitted tightly together with seams but no gaps, e.g. a paved pedestrian street.

LCH-1_6_3.label: Permeable Paving, Grass Pavers
LCH-1_6_3.tip: Paving pieces laid with small gaps so rainwater can soak into the ground, e.g. grass pavers in a car park.

LCH-1_6_4.label: Tiles
LCH-1_6_4.tip: Paving or roofing laid as tiles, which may partly overlap, e.g. a tiled roof.

LCH-1_7.label: Building Greening Type
LCH-1_7.tip: Groups types of vegetation grown on buildings, mainly on roofs and possibly on walls.

LCH-1_7_1.label: Greened Roof
LCH-1_7_1.tip: A roof covered with growing plants, e.g. a green roof on an office building.

LCH-1_7_1_1.label: Low Growing Roof Vegetation
LCH-1_7_1_1.tip: A green roof with low plants such as herbs, mosses, lichens or dwarf shrubs.

LCH-1_7_1_2.label: High Growing Roof Vegetation
LCH-1_7_1_2.tip: A green roof with taller woody plants such as trees and bushes, often forming a roof garden.

LCH-1_8.label: Transportation Network Characteristics
LCH-1_8.tip: Groups details that describe transport areas, such as types of roads and paths and types of harbours.

LCH-1_8_1.label: Road Network Type
LCH-1_8_1.tip: Groups types of roads and paths by their main use, from highways to footpaths and cycle lanes.

LCH-1_8_1_1.label: Fast Transit Road, Highway
LCH-1_8_1_1.tip: Roads built for fast long-distance traffic, e.g. motorways and highways.

LCH-1_8_1_2.label: Pedestrian Zone
LCH-1_8_1_2.tip: An area reserved for people on foot, sometimes bicycles, where motor traffic is banned or limited, e.g. a shopping street.

LCH-1_8_1_3.label: Associated Walk- Or Cycleway
LCH-1_8_1_3.tip: A footpath or cycle lane running alongside a road, sometimes separated from it by a narrow green strip.

LCH-1_8_1_4.label: Walk- and Cycleway
LCH-1_8_1_4.tip: A path shared by walkers and cyclists on its own route, away from roads.

LCH-1_8_1_5.label: Cycleway
LCH-1_8_1_5.tip: A path or lane reserved for bicycles only, with no pedestrians or cars, e.g. a separate bike lane.

LCH-1_8_1_6.label: Walkway
LCH-1_8_1_6.tip: A path meant only for people on foot, e.g. a footpath.

LCH-1_8_1_7.label: Open Square
LCH-1_8_1_7.tip: An open, often rectangular or round space in the street network, e.g. a town square or a large roundabout.

LCH-1_8_4.label: Harbour Type
LCH-1_8_4.tip: Groups types of port areas where ships and boats dock, load and unload, e.g. cargo ports, marinas and shipyards.

LCH-1_8_4_1.label: Cargo Port
LCH-1_8_4_1.tip: A port where traded goods are shipped in and out, usually with container terminals.

LCH-1_8_4_2.label: Passenger Port
LCH-1_8_4_2.tip: A port where people board and leave ships, e.g. a ferry or cruise terminal.

LCH-1_8_4_3.label: Fishing Port
LCH-1_8_4_3.tip: A port used by fishing boats bringing in their catch from the sea.

LCH-1_8_4_4.label: Naval Port
LCH-1_8_4_4.tip: A port that serves military ships, e.g. a navy base harbour.

LCH-1_8_4_5.label: Marina
LCH-1_8_4_5.tip: A harbour for yachts and sport boats used for recreation and leisure.

LCH-1_8_4_6.label: Local Multifunctional Harbour
LCH-1_8_4_6.tip: A local harbour not limited to one kind of vessel, serving several purposes at once.

LCH-1_8_4_7.label: Shipyard
LCH-1_8_4_7.tip: An area by the sea or a river where ships are built, maintained or repaired, either afloat or in a dry dock.

LCH-1_8_4_8.label: Jetty
LCH-1_8_4_8.tip: A long structure reaching out from the shore where vessels dock to load, unload or let passengers on and off.

LCH-2.label: Physical Characteristics
LCH-2.tip: Groups physical properties of the land itself, such as ground that stays permanently frozen.

LCH-2_1.label: Permafrost Zone
LCH-2_1.tip: Areas where the ground stays frozen for at least two years in a row, found in polar regions or high mountains.

LCH-3.label: Biotic Vegetation Characteristics
LCH-3.tip: Groups details describing plants and vegetation, e.g. leaf shape, whether leaves fall, lifespan, growth form and species origin.

LCH-3_1.label: Leaf Form
LCH-3_1.tip: Groups the basic leaf shapes used to tell trees and shrubs apart, e.g. needle leaves or broad leaves.

LCH-3_1_1.label: Needle Leaved
LCH-3_1_1.tip: Trees and shrubs with thin, needle-shaped leaves, e.g. pine, spruce or fir.

LCH-3_1_2.label: Broad Leaved
LCH-3_1_2.tip: Plants with broad, flat leaves, e.g. oak, beech or maple.

LCH-3_1_3.label: Palm Leaved
LCH-3_1_3.tip: Plants with the large fan- or feather-shaped leaves typical of palms, e.g. palm trees.

LCH-3_1_4.label: Non-Leafy
LCH-3_1_4.tip: Plants that have no leaves at all, e.g. many cacti that use green stems instead.

LCH-3_2.label: Foliage Persistence
LCH-3_2.tip: Groups plants by whether they shed their leaves or needles each season or keep them for several years.

LCH-3_2_1.label: Evergreen
LCH-3_2_1.tip: Plants that keep their leaves or needles for several years, e.g. spruce or holly.

LCH-3_2_2.label: Deciduous
LCH-3_2_2.tip: Plants that lose their leaves or needles at the end of each growing cycle, usually every year, e.g. beech or larch.

LCH-3_2_2_1.label: Winter Deciduous
LCH-3_2_2_1.tip: Plants that drop their leaves each year to cope with freezing winter temperatures, e.g. oak or birch.

LCH-3_2_2_2.label: Summer Deciduous
LCH-3_2_2_2.tip: Plants that drop their leaves each year before or during hot summers to avoid drying out.

LCH-3_3.label: Leaf Anatomy
LCH-3_3.tip: Groups features of the leaf's outer structure, such as how its surface or skin is built.

LCH-3_3_1.label: Sclerophyllous
LCH-3_3_1.tip: Plants with small, hard, leathery or waxy leaves adapted to long dry and hot periods, e.g. olive trees or cork oaks.

LCH-3_4.label: Phenological Plant Life Span
LCH-3_4.tip: Groups plants by how long they live, from one season to many years.

LCH-3_4_1.label: Annual Plant
LCH-3_4_1.tip: A plant that completes its whole life cycle within one growing season, e.g. many cereals or summer flowers.

LCH-3_4_2.label: Biennial Plant
LCH-3_4_2.tip: A plant whose life cycle spans two years, flowering and setting seed in the second year.

LCH-3_4_3.label: Perennial Plant
LCH-3_4_3.tip: A plant that survives unfavourable seasons such as winter and lives more than two years.

LCH-3_4_4.label: Ephemeral Plant
LCH-3_4_4.tip: A plant that runs through several life cycles in one growing season and can multiply quickly.

LCH-3_5.label: Plant Location
LCH-3_5.tip: Groups plants by where they grow: on land, on other plants, under water or at the water surface.

LCH-3_5_1.label: Terrestrial Plant
LCH-3_5_1.tip: Plants growing on solid ground, including wetland plants like reeds that stand in water.

LCH-3_5_2.label: Epiphyte Plant
LCH-3_5_2.tip: A plant that grows on another plant for support, taking moisture and nutrients from air, rain or debris rather than its host.

LCH-3_5_3.label: Aquatic Submerged Plant
LCH-3_5_3.tip: Water plants living mainly below the surface without reaching it, e.g. algae.

LCH-3_5_4.label: Aquatic Emergent Plant
LCH-3_5_4.tip: Water plants that mainly float on the water surface, e.g. water lilies.

LCH-3_6.label: Growth Form, Habit
LCH-3_6.tip: Groups the overall shapes plants grow into, describing how their stems and branches are arranged.

LCH-3_6_1.label: Erect Growth, Single Stem
LCH-3_6_1.tip: A woody plant with one main upright stem, as in a typical tree.

LCH-3_6_2.label: Open, Spreading, Dense Growth, Multi-Stem
LCH-3_6_2.tip: A woody plant with several stems growing from the ground upward and outward, e.g. bushes and shrubs.

LCH-3_6_3.label: Prostrate, Creaping
LCH-3_6_3.tip: Plants whose branches or shoots lie on or just above the ground and spread sideways rather than upright.

LCH-3_6_4.label: Clump-Forming
LCH-3_6_4.tip: Plants growing as a compact mound or thicket with shoots spreading out from the centre, e.g. bamboos, sedges or some grasses.

LCH-3_6_5.label: Cushion, Mat-Forming
LCH-3_6_5.tip: Low, compact, pillow-like or mat-forming plants with tightly packed branches, found in alpine and arctic environments.

LCH-3_6_6.label: Climbing
LCH-3_6_6.tip: Plants that climb on other plants or objects for support because they lack strong stems, e.g. ivy or grapevine.

LCH-3_7.label: Raunkiaer Life Form
LCH-3_7.tip: Groups plants by Raunkiaer's system, which classifies them by where their buds survive the unfavourable season, e.g. high above ground or underground.

LCH-3_7_1.label: Phanerophyte
LCH-3_7_1.tip: A Raunkiaer life form for plants whose resting buds sit well above the ground on woody stems, e.g. trees and tall shrubs.

LCH-3_7_2.label: Epiphyte
LCH-3_7_2.tip: A Raunkiaer life form for plants that grow on other plants rather than rooting in the soil.

LCH-3_7_3.label: Chamaephyte
LCH-3_7_3.tip: A Raunkiaer life form for low plants whose resting buds sit close above the ground, e.g. dwarf shrubs.

LCH-3_7_4.label: Hemicryptophyte
LCH-3_7_4.tip: A Raunkiaer life form for plants whose resting buds sit right at the soil surface, e.g. many grasses.

LCH-3_7_5.label: Cryptophyte
LCH-3_7_5.tip: A Raunkiaer life form for plants whose resting buds survive below ground or under water, e.g. bulbs.

LCH-3_7_6.label: Therophyte
LCH-3_7_6.tip: A Raunkiaer life form for plants that survive the unfavourable season only as seeds, e.g. annual herbs.

LCH-3_7_7.label: Aerophyte
LCH-3_7_7.tip: A Raunkiaer life form for plants that live in the air without roots in the soil, taking water and nutrients from the air.

LCH-3_8.label: Vegetation Cover Transition
LCH-3_8.tip: Groups the direction vegetation cover is changing in: either recovering naturally or degrading over time.

LCH-3_8_1.label: Natural Succession
LCH-3_8_1.tip: Land where vegetation is regrowing on its own through natural succession, e.g. abandoned fields turning into scrub.

LCH-3_8_2.label: Vegetation Degradation
LCH-3_8_2.tip: Land where the vegetation cover is getting poorer or thinner over time.

LCH-3_9.label: Plant Species Origin
LCH-3_9.tip: Groups plants by their origin relative to where they grow now, e.g. native, introduced, invasive or genetically modified.

LCH-3_9_1.label: Native Plant
LCH-3_9_1.tip: A plant species that has naturally grown in this region for a long time, though not necessarily only here.

LCH-3_9_2.label: Non-Native Plant
LCH-3_9_2.tip: A plant species that is not normally found in this region.

LCH-3_9_3.label: Endemic Plant
LCH-3_9_3.tip: A plant species found only in this particular region and nowhere else, at any scale from a tiny habitat to a continent.

LCH-3_9_4.label: Invasive Plant
LCH-3_9_4.tip: A plant from elsewhere that is spreading into a new area, often helped by human transport, and crowding out native plants.

LCH-3_9_5.label: Migratory Plant
LCH-3_9_5.tip: A plant species gradually moving into a neighbouring area because conditions in its original habitat are changing, e.g. due to climate.

LCH-3_9_6.label: Genetically Modified Plant
LCH-3_9_6.tip: A plant whose genes have been altered, e.g. crops modified for higher yield or drought resistance.

LCH-3_10.label: Plant Species Type
LCH-3_10.tip: Groups ways to record which plant species are present, following the INSPIRE species distribution standard.

LCH-3_10_1.label: Plant Species
LCH-3_10_1.tip: Records the name of the specific plant species growing in an area.

LCH-3_11.label: Plant Community Type
LCH-3_11.tip: Groups ways to record which plant community grows in an area; still being finalised, possibly following the European Vegetation Survey scheme.

LCH-3_11_1.label: Plant Community
LCH-3_11_1.tip: Records the plant community, meaning a typical group of species growing together, e.g. a beech forest community.

LCH-3_12.label: Plant Growing Season
LCH-3_12.tip: Groups details about the natural growing season of wild and local plants. Crop seasons are recorded elsewhere.

LCH-3_12_1.label: Plant Growing Season Ongoing
LCH-3_12_1.tip: Indicates whether the natural growing season of a plant or plant community is currently under way. Does not cover crop seasons.

LCH-3_13.label: Crown Cover Density
LCH-3_13.tip: Measures how much of an area is covered from above by tree or bush crowns, given as a percentage (%).

LCH-4.label: Water Characteristics
LCH-4.tip: Groups details that describe water surfaces or relate to water, such as how natural a water body is and how often it holds water.

LCH-4_1.label: Water Body Formation
LCH-4_1.tip: Groups water bodies by how natural they are, from untouched rivers and lakes to fully man-made canals.

LCH-4_1_1.label: Natural Water Body
LCH-4_1_1.tip: A river or lake in its natural state, with no artificial banks and no dams or weirs controlling its flow.

LCH-4_1_2.label: Controlled, Regulated, Heavily Modified Water Body
LCH-4_1_2.tip: A river or lake shaped by man-made structures that hold its banks or control its water level, e.g. most navigable rivers.

LCH-4_1_3.label: Man-Made Water Body
LCH-4_1_3.tip: A fully artificial water body that would not exist without people, e.g. a shipping canal or irrigation reservoir.

LCH-4_2.label: Hydrological Water Regime
LCH-4_2.tip: Groups inland waters by how often and how long they hold or carry water, e.g. permanent or seasonal. Not used for sea or tidal areas.

LCH-4_2_1.label: Dry Water Regime
LCH-4_2_1.tip: A riverbed or lake bed that is normally dry, with water flowing only rarely after heavy rain, e.g. a wadi in a desert region.

LCH-4_2_2.label: Ephemeral, Episodic Water Regime
LCH-4_2_2.tip: Water appears only during or after rain and then stops flowing again, though some seasonal pattern may still be seen, e.g. a stream that runs after storms.

LCH-4_2_3.label: Intermittent, Seasonal Water Regime
LCH-4_2_3.tip: Water is present for part of every year, usually in the wet or snowmelt season, e.g. a stream that dries up each summer.

LCH-4_2_4.label: Perennial Water Regime
LCH-4_2_4.tip: Water is present all year round, even if the level rises and falls, e.g. a large river or permanent lake.

LCH-4_3.label: Water Dynamics
LCH-4_3.tip: Groups descriptions of whether water in a water body flows or stays still, from fast-moving rivers to stagnant ponds.

LCH-4_3_1.label: Running Water
LCH-4_3_1.tip: Water that keeps moving with a current, so it is constantly renewed and can wear away or deposit ground material, e.g. a river or creek.

LCH-4_3_2.label: Almost Standing Water
LCH-4_3_2.tip: Water that moves so slowly it causes little or no erosion, usually on very flat land, e.g. a canal or drainage ditch.

LCH-4_3_3.label: Standing Water
LCH-4_3_3.tip: Still water with no current at all, e.g. a lake, pond or puddle.

LCH-4_4.label: Soil Moisture Regime, Wetness
LCH-4_4.tip: Groups classes describing how wet or dry the soil is, from land covered by shallow water to desert soils with almost no moisture.

LCH-4_4_1.label: Aquatic, Water At Surface
LCH-4_4_1.tip: Land that is not a water body but is so wet that shallow water covers its surface, e.g. parts of a marsh or bog.

LCH-4_4_2.label: Waterlogged, Saturated Ground
LCH-4_4_2.tip: Soil soaked with water so that nearly all air spaces are filled, often because groundwater is high or rain is frequent.

LCH-4_4_3.label: Wet
LCH-4_4_3.tip: Soil that stays wet all year, with water filling many pores but some air still present, often fed by groundwater close to the surface.

LCH-4_4_4.label: Seasonally Wet
LCH-4_4_4.tip: Soil that is wet only during part of the year, for example in a rainy season or after seasonal flooding.

LCH-4_4_5.label: Mesic
LCH-4_4_5.tip: Soil with a steady, moderate supply of moisture, enough for plants to avoid drought stress; typical of temperate regions with evenly spread rainfall.

LCH-4_4_6.label: Semi-Dry
LCH-4_4_6.tip: Soil that alternates between rainy and dry spells, with dry periods dominating; water drains away quickly and little is held for plants.

LCH-4_4_7.label: Dry
LCH-4_4_7.tip: Soil where hardly any moisture is available to plants through the year, and droughts may last years; only hardy vegetation survives.

LCH-4_4_8.label: Very Dry
LCH-4_4_8.tip: Soil so dry that no vegetation can grow and almost no life is present, as in true deserts.

LCH-4_4_9.label: Xeric
LCH-4_4_9.tip: Soil moisture typical of a Mediterranean climate, with cool, wet winters and hot, dry summers.

LCH-4_5.label: Wetness Source
LCH-4_5.tip: Groups the possible origins of the water that makes land wet, such as rain, surface water or groundwater.

LCH-4_5_1.label: Rainfed Source
LCH-4_5_1.tip: Land whose wetness comes from rainfall.

LCH-4_5_2.label: Surface Water Source
LCH-4_5_2.tip: Land whose wetness comes from surface water flowing in, e.g. from a nearby river or runoff.

LCH-4_5_3.label: Subterranean, Groundwater Source
LCH-4_5_3.tip: Land whose wetness comes from groundwater rising up through the soil from below.

LCH-4_6.label: Salinity
LCH-4_6.tip: Groups classes for how salty water or soil is, from salt-saturated brine to practically salt-free rainwater. Usually given in parts per thousand.

LCH-4_6_1.label: Brine
LCH-4_6_1.tip: Water that is saturated or nearly saturated with salt, at 50 parts per thousand or more, e.g. the Dead Sea.

LCH-4_6_2.label: Saline
LCH-4_6_2.tip: Salty water as found in the oceans and salt lakes, with 30 to 50 parts per thousand of salt, e.g. the Atlantic Ocean.

LCH-4_6_3.label: Brackish
LCH-4_6_3.tip: Water saltier than fresh water but less salty than the sea (5 to 30 parts per thousand), e.g. estuaries, lagoons or the Baltic Sea.

LCH-4_6_4.label: Fresh
LCH-4_6_4.tip: Water with very little salt (0.1 to 0.5 parts per thousand), e.g. most rivers and groundwater; drinkable water lies at the low end.

LCH-4_6_5.label: Ultra Fresh
LCH-4_6_5.tip: Water that is practically free of salt, like rain, snow or dew before it picks up other substances.

LCH-4_7.label: pH Value
LCH-4_7.tip: Measures how acidic or alkaline water is, on a scale from 0 (acidic) to 14 (alkaline), where 7 is neutral like pure water.

LCH-4_8.label: Tidal Phenomena
LCH-4_8.tip: Groups characteristics of coastal areas that are regularly flooded and drained by the tides.

LCH-4_8_1.label: Tidal Influence
LCH-4_8_1.tip: Records whether a piece of land is affected by the tides, optionally with the typical rise and fall of the water level.

LCH-4_8_2.label: Tidal Range
LCH-4_8_2.tip: Measures the height difference between low tide and high tide at a location, in meters.

LCH-4_9.label: Groundwater
LCH-4_9.tip: Groups characteristics of groundwater, the water held underground in soil and rock.

LCH-4_9_1.label: Groundwater Table Level
LCH-4_9_1.tip: Measures how far below the ground surface the groundwater (water table) lies, in meters.

LCH-4_10.label: Snow Characteristics
LCH-4_10.tip: Groups characteristics describing surfaces covered by snow.

LCH-4_10_1.label: Snow Height
LCH-4_10_1.tip: Measures the depth of snow lying on the ground, in meters.

LCH-4_11.label: Ice Characteristics
LCH-4_11.tip: Groups characteristics of surfaces covered by ice, on land or water; currently a placeholder for future entries.

LCH-5.label: Land Management
LCH-5.tip: Groups information on how people manage and work the land, such as farming methods, cultivation practices and what crops are grown.

LCH-5_1.label: Agricultural Land Management
LCH-5_1.tip: Groups characteristics of how farmland is managed, including cultivation forms, farming practices, installations, field work and crop types.

LCH-5_1_1.label: Agricultural Cultivation Form
LCH-5_1_1.tip: Groups the main forms farmland takes, shaped by the crops grown and how the land is worked: cropland and managed permanent grassland.

LCH-5_1_1_1.label: Cropland
LCH-5_1_1_1.tip: Farmland used to plant, grow and harvest crops, covering both fields of annual crops and orchards or vineyards; managed grassland is separate.

LCH-5_1_1_1_1.label: Arable Crop Land
LCH-5_1_1_1_1.tip: Fields that are ploughed or prepared for sowing annual crops, often in rotation, e.g. wheat fields; also includes fallow land and rice fields.

LCH-5_1_1_1_2.label: Permanent Crop Land
LCH-5_1_1_1_2.tip: Land planted with long-lived, mostly woody crops, often in regular rows, e.g. vineyards, olive groves or fruit orchards.

LCH-5_1_1_2.label: Managed Permanent Grassland
LCH-5_1_1_2.tip: Grassland kept for several years in a row to grow grass or other herbaceous plants for animal feed or energy, e.g. a hay meadow; it is rarely ploughed.

LCH-5_1_2.label: Cultivation Practice
LCH-5_1_2.tip: Groups the overall farming approaches applied to land, such as crop rotation, plantations or agroforestry, including cropping cycles and plant arrangement.

LCH-5_1_2_1.label: Crop Rotation
LCH-5_1_2_1.tip: Different crops are grown on the same field in a planned sequence over several years; applies mainly to land with annual crops.

LCH-5_1_2_2.label: No Crop Rotation
LCH-5_1_2_2.tip: The same crop is grown on a field year after year over a long period, rather than alternating crops.

LCH-5_1_2_3.label: Plantation
LCH-5_1_2_3.tip: Large estates growing cash crops in rows using industrialised methods aimed at high yields, e.g. a large fruit plantation with plants tied to wires.

LCH-5_1_2_4.label: Extensive Cultivation Practice
LCH-5_1_2_4.tip: Low-intensity farming, for example traditional orchards of scattered fruit, nut or olive trees, often with grass underneath and valuable for wildlife.

LCH-5_1_2_5.label: Agroforestry
LCH-5_1_2_5.tip: Trees combined with farming on the same land, with livestock grazing or crops grown between scattered trees, e.g. the Spanish dehesa.

LCH-5_1_2_6.label: Shifting Cultivation
LCH-5_1_2_6.tip: Slash-and-burn farming, mainly in the tropics: forest is cleared and burnt, cropped for a few years, then left to regrow before the cycle repeats.

LCH-5_1_2_7.label: Intercropping
LCH-5_1_2_7.tip: Growing two or more crops together on the same field at the same time to use space better, e.g. a tall nut tree crop with a shade-tolerant crop below.

LCH-5_1_2_8.label: Kitchen Garden
LCH-5_1_2_8.tip: Small plots of fruit, vegetables and herbs grown mainly for the household's own use rather than for sale.

LCH-5_1_2_9.label: Paddy Field Cultivation
LCH-5_1_2_9.tip: Rice grown on fields that are flooded for part of the season; the only rice-growing method used in Europe.

LCH-5_1_3.label: Cultivation Installation
LCH-5_1_3.tip: Groups technical installations used on farmland to boost plant growth, raise yields or protect crops, such as greenhouses or protective nets.

LCH-5_1_3_1.label: Greenhouse Under Glass or Foil
LCH-5_1_3_1.tip: Crops grown under permanent glass or mounted plastic, where the farmer controls temperature, light and water, e.g. a tomato greenhouse.

LCH-5_1_3_2.label: Under Foil On Ground
LCH-5_1_3_2.tip: Crops covered by plastic sheeting lying directly on the ground or plants, creating a warm, sheltered microclimate, e.g. early strawberries or asparagus.

LCH-5_1_3_3.label: Plantation Protection Net
LCH-5_1_3_3.tip: Nets stretched over crops, mostly orchards or other permanent crops, to protect them from things like birds or hail.

LCH-5_1_3_4.label: Espalier, Trellis, Lattice
LCH-5_1_3_4.tip: Fruit trees or shrubs trained flat along a frame by pruning and tying their branches, so they grow in neat lines.

LCH-5_1_3_5.label: Hydroculture
LCH-5_1_3_5.tip: Growing plants without soil, with roots in a nutrient-rich water solution, sometimes supported by an inert material, e.g. hydroponic lettuce.

LCH-5_1_3_6.label: Vertical Farming
LCH-5_1_3_6.tip: Indoor growing of crops on several stacked levels, in a multi-storey building or on racks inside a greenhouse.

LCH-5_1_4.label: Cultivation Measure and Activities
LCH-5_1_4.tip: Groups the routine field work done to keep farmland fertile and productive, from planting to harvest, such as ploughing, fertilizing and irrigation.

LCH-5_1_4_1.label: Ploughing and Tillage
LCH-5_1_4_1.tip: Groups options describing whether a field is ploughed and, if known, in which direction relative to the slope.

LCH-5_1_4_1_1.label: No Ploughing
LCH-5_1_4_1_1.tip: The field is not ploughed; the soil is left undisturbed rather than being turned over before sowing.

LCH-5_1_4_1_2.label: Ploughing Applied, Direction Unspecified
LCH-5_1_4_1_2.tip: The field is ploughed, but the direction of ploughing is not known or not recorded.

LCH-5_1_4_1_3.label: Ploughing Across The Slope
LCH-5_1_4_1_3.tip: Furrows run along the slope, following the contour lines, which helps slow water running downhill.

LCH-5_1_4_1_4.label: Ploughing Oblique Direction
LCH-5_1_4_1_4.tip: Furrows run diagonally across the slope, neither along the contours nor straight downhill.

LCH-5_1_4_1_5.label: Ploughing in Direction of Slope
LCH-5_1_4_1_5.tip: Furrows run straight up and down the slope, the way water would flow downhill.

LCH-5_1_4_2.label: Fertilization
LCH-5_1_4_2.tip: Groups options for whether and how land is fertilized, i.e. given nutrients from plant residues, manure or chemical products to keep soil fertile.

LCH-5_1_4_2_2.label: Fertilization Applied, Type Unspecified
LCH-5_1_4_2_2.tip: The land is fertilized, but the kind of fertilizer used is not known.

LCH-5_1_4_2_3.label: Organic Fertilizer
LCH-5_1_4_2_3.tip: Natural fertilizer such as plant material or animal manure spread on or ploughed into the field.

LCH-5_1_4_2_3_1.label: Animal Manure
LCH-5_1_4_2_3_1.tip: Animal dung or manure spread on or ploughed into fields as a natural fertilizer.

LCH-5_1_4_2_3_2.label: Green Manure
LCH-5_1_4_2_3_2.tip: Plant material grown on or brought to a field and ploughed in to feed the soil, e.g. a cover crop sown between two main crops.

LCH-5_1_4_2_4.label: Synthetic Fertilizer
LCH-5_1_4_2_4.tip: Factory-made fertilizers produced from minerals by industrial chemical processes, e.g. nitrogen fertilizer pellets.

LCH-5_1_4_3.label: Weed Control
LCH-5_1_4_3.tip: Groups options for whether and how unwanted plants competing with a crop for water, light and nutrients are controlled.

LCH-5_1_4_3_1.label: No Weed Control
LCH-5_1_4_3_1.tip: No measures are taken against weeds on this land.

LCH-5_1_4_3_2.label: Weed Control Applied, Method Unspecified
LCH-5_1_4_3_2.tip: Weeds are controlled, but the method used is not known.

LCH-5_1_4_3_3.label: Mechanical or Biological Weed Control
LCH-5_1_4_3_3.tip: Weeds are controlled physically, e.g. by tilling, or biologically, using their natural enemies.

LCH-5_1_4_3_4.label: Chemical Weed Control
LCH-5_1_4_3_4.tip: Weeds are controlled with chemicals such as herbicides.

LCH-5_1_4_4.label: Pest Control
LCH-5_1_4_4.tip: Groups options for whether and how crops are protected from insects or other organisms that damage them and reduce yields.

LCH-5_1_4_4_1.label: No Pest Control
LCH-5_1_4_4_1.tip: No measures are taken against pests on this land.

LCH-5_1_4_4_2.label: Pest Control Applied, Method Unspecified
LCH-5_1_4_4_2.tip: Pests are controlled, but the method used is not known.

LCH-5_1_4_4_3.label: Mechanical or Biological Pest Control
LCH-5_1_4_4_3.tip: Pests are controlled physically, e.g. with traps, or biologically, using their natural enemies.

LCH-5_1_4_4_4.label: Chemical Pest Control
LCH-5_1_4_4_4.tip: Pests are controlled with chemicals such as pesticides.

LCH-5_1_4_5.label: Irrigation
LCH-5_1_4_5.tip: Groups options for whether land is artificially watered to help crops grow, and by which method, such as sprinklers or drip lines.

LCH-5_1_4_5_1.label: No Irrigation
LCH-5_1_4_5_1.tip: The land is not artificially watered; crops depend on natural water only.

LCH-5_1_4_5_2.label: Irrigation Applied, Method Unspecified
LCH-5_1_4_5_2.tip: The land is irrigated, but the watering method is not known.

LCH-5_1_4_5_3.label: Gravity Surface Irrigation
LCH-5_1_4_5_3.tip: Water flows over the field by gravity, through small channels or furrows between crops or by flooding the whole plot.

LCH-5_1_4_5_4.label: Sprinkler Irrigation
LCH-5_1_4_5_4.tip: Water sprayed under pressure over the field like artificial rain, from mobile or fixed sprinklers.

LCH-5_1_4_5_5.label: Irrigation Carousel
LCH-5_1_4_5_5.tip: A long watering arm rotates around a central point, spraying water in a circle; it creates the round green fields seen from the air.

LCH-5_1_4_5_6.label: Drip Irrigation
LCH-5_1_4_5_6.tip: Water delivered drop by drop to each plant through thin perforated tubes on the ground, or as a fine mist from micro-sprayers.

LCH-5_1_4_5_7.label: Subsurface Drip Irrigation
LCH-5_1_4_5_7.tip: Water delivered to plants through perforated tubes or tapes buried underground, at or below root level.

LCH-5_1_4_5_8.label: Manual Irrigation
LCH-5_1_4_5_8.tip: Plants are watered by hand, e.g. with a hose or watering can.

LCH-5_1_4_6.label: Irrigation Water Source
LCH-5_1_4_6.tip: Groups the places where irrigation water is taken from, such as wells, reservoirs or rivers.

LCH-5_1_4_6_1.label: Groundwater
LCH-5_1_4_6_1.tip: Irrigation water pumped from underground water layers, usually through wells.

LCH-5_1_4_6_2.label: Reservoir
LCH-5_1_4_6_2.tip: Irrigation water taken from a stored body of water, e.g. a dammed artificial lake, a natural lake or a rainwater cistern.

LCH-5_1_4_6_3.label: Water Course
LCH-5_1_4_6_3.tip: Irrigation water taken directly from a flowing river, stream or creek.

LCH-5_1_4_7.label: Drainage
LCH-5_1_4_7.tip: Groups options for whether and how excess water is removed from farmland through drains or ditches, lowering the groundwater level.

LCH-5_1_4_7_1.label: No Drainage
LCH-5_1_4_7_1.tip: No drainage is carried out on this land.

LCH-5_1_4_7_2.label: Drainage Applied, Method Unspecified
LCH-5_1_4_7_2.tip: The land appears to be drained, but the method is not known.

LCH-5_1_4_7_3.label: Open Ditch Drainage
LCH-5_1_4_7_3.tip: Land drained by long open ditches or trenches into which water seeps from the surrounding ground.

LCH-5_1_4_7_4.label: Subsurface Tube Drainage
LCH-5_1_4_7_4.tip: Land drained by perforated pipes buried beneath the surface, which collect water and carry it away.

LCH-5_1_4_7_5.label: Filled Ditch Drainage
LCH-5_1_4_7_5.tip: Land drained by trenches filled with loose material such as gravel, level with the ground so they can be crossed easily.

LCH-5_1_4_8.label: Mowing
LCH-5_1_4_8.tip: Groups information on mowing a piece of land, especially how often it is cut during the year.

LCH-5_1_4_8_1.label: Mowing Intensity
LCH-5_1_4_8_1.tip: Groups classes describing how intensively land is mowed, from no mowing to several cuts per year.

LCH-5_1_4_8_1_2.label: Mowing Applied, Frequency Unspecified
LCH-5_1_4_8_1_2.tip: The plot is mowed, but how often is not known.

LCH-5_1_4_8_1_3.label: Extensive Mowing
LCH-5_1_4_8_1_3.tip: Low-intensity mowing: the plot is cut once a year, e.g. a traditional hay meadow.

LCH-5_1_4_8_1_4.label: Medium Intensity Mowing
LCH-5_1_4_8_1_4.tip: The plot is mowed twice a year.

LCH-5_1_4_8_1_5.label: Intensive Mowing
LCH-5_1_4_8_1_5.tip: The plot is mowed more than twice a year.

LCH-5_1_4_8_2.label: Mowing Frequency
LCH-5_1_4_8_2.tip: Records how many times per year a piece of land is mowed, given as a count.

LCH-5_1_4_9.label: Shrub Clearance
LCH-5_1_4_9.tip: Removing bushes and young trees from grassland to stop it turning into scrub or woodland, keeping it open, often for grazing.

LCH-5_1_4_10.label: Biomass Burning
LCH-5_1_4_10.tip: Burning off unwanted plants on farmland to control growth; the ashes left behind also enrich the soil.

LCH-5_1_4_11.label: Liming
LCH-5_1_4_11.tip: Spreading lime (calcium carbonate) on land to make the soil less acidic; used mainly in conifer forests but also on farmland.

LCH-5_1_4_12.label: Pruning
LCH-5_1_4_12.tip: Selectively cutting branches, twigs, buds or roots to shape plants and improve health or harvest, e.g. trimming fruit trees or vines.

LCH-5_1_4_13.label: Set Aside Parcel
LCH-5_1_4_13.tip: A farm plot temporarily taken out of crop production for one or more seasons to let the soil recover, sometimes as part of a crop rotation.

LCH-5_1_5.label: Cultivation Purpose
LCH-5_1_5.tip: Groups the reasons crops are grown, such as for food, animal feed, industry or energy; the same crop can serve different purposes on different fields.

LCH-5_1_5_1.label: Alimentary Crop
LCH-5_1_5_1.tip: Crops grown as food for people, e.g. vegetables, cereals or fruit, whether eaten fresh or processed. Animal feed crops are not included.

LCH-5_1_5_1_1.label: Grain Production Crop
LCH-5_1_5_1_1.tip: Crops grown to harvest cereal grains for human food, e.g. wheat for bread.

LCH-5_1_5_1_2.label: Table Fruit Crop
LCH-5_1_5_1_2.tip: Crops grown so their whole fruits can be eaten, e.g. apples or table grapes.

LCH-5_1_5_1_3.label: Liquefication, Fermentation or Brewing of Crop
LCH-5_1_5_1_3.tip: Crops grown to be pressed, fermented or brewed, e.g. into juice, wine, edible oil or flavour extracts.

LCH-5_1_5_2.label: Fodder Crop
LCH-5_1_5_2.tip: Crops grown to feed farm animals, e.g. fodder beet, silage maize or alfalfa.

LCH-5_1_5_2_1.label: Harvested For Silage
LCH-5_1_5_2_1.tip: Fodder crops stored after harvest in a silo or sealed plastic-covered pile, where fermentation preserves them as silage for animals.

LCH-5_1_5_2_2.label: Harvested For Dry Fodder
LCH-5_1_5_2_2.tip: Grass or similar plants mowed and left on the field to dry into hay or straw, a way of preserving animal feed.

LCH-5_1_5_2_3.label: Harvested Green For Direct Forage
LCH-5_1_5_2_3.tip: Grass or similar plants cut fresh and green and fed to animals straight away.

LCH-5_1_5_2_4.label: Temporary Grasses And Grazings
LCH-5_1_5_2_4.tip: Grass or grass mixtures sown for grazing, hay or silage as part of a crop rotation, lasting from one to under five years before being ploughed up.

LCH-5_1_5_3.label: Industrial Crop
LCH-5_1_5_3.tip: Crops grown as raw materials for industry or manufacturing, e.g. cotton or flax for linen.

LCH-5_1_5_4.label: Energy Crop
LCH-5_1_5_4.tip: Crops grown to produce energy, e.g. maize fed into a biogas plant.

LCH-5_1_5_4_1.label: Bio Gas Crop
LCH-5_1_5_4_1.tip: Crops grown to be fed into biogas plants for energy production.

LCH-5_1_5_4_2.label: Liquid Bio Fuel Crop
LCH-5_1_5_4_2.tip: Crops grown to make liquid biofuels, e.g. rapeseed oil, or bioethanol from sugar cane or maize.

LCH-5_1_5_4_3.label: Solid Bio Fuel Crop
LCH-5_1_5_4_3.tip: Crops grown to produce solid biofuels, e.g. fast-growing trees harvested as energy wood.

LCH-5_1_5_5.label: Ornamental Plants
LCH-5_1_5_5.tip: Plants grown for decoration or landscaping, e.g. nursery trees and shrubs later planted in parks, gardens or public spaces.

LCH-5_1_5_6.label: Functional Crop
LCH-5_1_5_6.tip: Crops grown mainly for a useful function other than food, feed, industry or energy, such as protecting soil; can be combined with other purposes.

LCH-5_1_5_6_1.label: Soil Protective Cover Crop
LCH-5_1_5_6_1.tip: Crops grown to cover and protect soil from erosion or drying out.

LCH-5_1_5_6_2.label: Soil Nutrient Storage Crop
LCH-5_1_5_6_2.tip: Crops grown to enrich the soil with nutrients such as natural nitrogen, e.g. clover.

LCH-5_1_5_6_3.label: Biodiversity Conservation Crop
LCH-5_1_5_6_3.tip: Crops grown to protect, preserve or restore biodiversity, e.g. flowering strips that support insects.

LCH-5_1_5_6_4.label: Carbon Sequestration Crop
LCH-5_1_5_6_4.tip: Crops grown mainly to take carbon dioxide out of the air and store it in plants or in the soil.

LCH-5_1_5_7.label: Seed Production Crop
LCH-5_1_5_7.tip: Crops grown to produce seeds for future sowing.

LCH-5_1_6.label: Crop Type
LCH-5_1_6.tip: Groups crops by their form or by the part of the plant that is harvested, such as cereals, pulses or root crops, rather than by their use.

LCH-5_1_6_1.label: Arable Crops
LCH-5_1_6_1.tip: Crops grown on ploughed fields, usually annually, grouped here into cereals, pulses, fodder legumes and root crops.

LCH-5_1_6_1_1.label: Cereals
LCH-5_1_6_1_1.tip: Grass-family crops grown for their grain, e.g. wheat, barley, maize or rice.

LCH-5_1_6_1_1_1.label: Common Wheat and Spelt
LCH-5_1_6_1_1_1.tip: Ordinary bread wheat and the closely related older grain spelt.

LCH-5_1_6_1_1_2.label: Durum Wheat
LCH-5_1_6_1_1_2.tip: Hard wheat, the type mainly used to make pasta and semolina.

LCH-5_1_6_1_1_3.label: Rye
LCH-5_1_6_1_1_3.tip: A hardy cereal grain, used for example in rye bread.

LCH-5_1_6_1_1_4.label: Barley
LCH-5_1_6_1_1_4.tip: A cereal grain used for animal feed, malting and brewing beer.

LCH-5_1_6_1_1_5.label: Oats
LCH-5_1_6_1_1_5.tip: A cereal grain used for animal feed and foods such as porridge and oat flakes.

LCH-5_1_6_1_1_6.label: Maize
LCH-5_1_6_1_1_6.tip: Corn, a tall cereal crop grown for its grain cobs, as animal feed or for energy.

LCH-5_1_6_1_1_7.label: Rice
LCH-5_1_6_1_1_7.tip: A cereal grown for its grain, usually in flooded paddy fields.

LCH-5_1_6_1_1_8.label: Millet
LCH-5_1_6_1_1_8.tip: Small-seeded cereal grasses grown for grain, used for food and bird or animal feed.

LCH-5_1_6_1_1_9.label: Other Cereals
LCH-5_1_6_1_1_9.tip: Cereal crops not listed separately, e.g. triticale or sorghum.

LCH-5_1_6_1_2.label: Pulses and Protein Crops
LCH-5_1_6_1_2.tip: Legume crops grown for their protein-rich dry seeds, e.g. peas, beans, lentils or soya.

LCH-5_1_6_1_2_1.label: Peas
LCH-5_1_6_1_2_1.tip: Pea plants grown for their seeds, harvested dry or fresh.

LCH-5_1_6_1_2_2.label: Beans
LCH-5_1_6_1_2_2.tip: Bean plants grown for their seeds, e.g. field beans or kidney beans.

LCH-5_1_6_1_2_3.label: Lentils
LCH-5_1_6_1_2_3.tip: A legume crop grown for its small, lens-shaped edible seeds.

LCH-5_1_6_1_2_4.label: Sweet Lupins
LCH-5_1_6_1_2_4.tip: Lupin varieties low in bitter substances, grown for their protein-rich seeds used as food or animal feed.

LCH-5_1_6_1_2_5.label: Soya
LCH-5_1_6_1_2_5.tip: Soybeans, a legume grown for its protein- and oil-rich beans, used in food and animal feed.

LCH-5_1_6_1_2_6.label: Chickpeas
LCH-5_1_6_1_2_6.tip: A legume grown for its round edible seeds, used for example in hummus.

LCH-5_1_6_1_2_7.label: Peanuts
LCH-5_1_6_1_2_7.tip: Groundnuts, a legume whose pods ripen underground; despite the name, not a true nut.

LCH-5_1_6_1_2_8.label: Other Dry Pulses
LCH-5_1_6_1_2_8.tip: Legumes grown for dry seeds that are not listed separately, e.g. vetches or grass peas.

LCH-5_1_6_1_3.label: Clover, Vetch, Lupins, Lucerne
